subject: Supplier banking preference & invoice submission intake
messages:
From: Tom Alvarez <tom@greenlinesys.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodai.com>
Cc: accounts-payable@greenlinesys.com
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Supplier setup — banking options, remittance & invoice flow

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We want to get Greenline set up in your vendor system so we can start receiving POs and submit invoices. A few quick questions to make sure we send the right information: 

- Do you require ACH for US vendors or do you also accept wires? Any preferred bank fields (routing/account number vs IBAN for wires)?
- What email should we use for remittance advices (e.g., remits@greenlinesys.com vs a Redwood-specific email)?
- Is there a preferred PDF invoice template or a PO reference field we must include to avoid coding delays?
- Do you accept invoices via email, vendor portal upload, or via SFTP?

We have completed the W-9 (attached) and can return any vendor intake form you need. If helpful, I can schedule a short call Monday.

Thanks,
Tom Alvarez
Head of Finance Operations
Greenline Systems
Attachment: W9_Greenline.pdf (form)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodai.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom@greenlinesys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodai.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 11:04:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Supplier setup — banking options, remittance & invoice flow

Tom — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (Procurement) and Ben (Finance ops) so we can get you fully onboarded. High level answers below and an intake checklist attached.

Short answers:
- We prefer ACH for US payouts (faster, lower cost); we will process wires for one-off exceptions (international vendors or urgent invoices). For wires we need beneficiary name, account number, SWIFT, and intermediary bank if applicable.
- Please send remittance notices to ap-remits@redwoodai.com. You can continue to copy accounts-payable@greenlinesys.com on your side for tracking, but Redwood requires AP remits to parse and attach to invoices.
- Include the Redwood PO number clearly in the invoice's subject line and in the invoice body (PO: RWD-XXXX). We also prefer a single PDF per invoice and a PDF filename with your invoice number and date.
- Preferred submission: email to invoices@redwoodai.com is fine for most vendors. For high-volume suppliers we offer SFTP or portal upload — Marissa, can you confirm thresholds?

Attached: Redwood_vendor_form.pdf and a short PO_workflow_overview.pdf. Please fill out the vendor form and return with your banking details. If you prefer, we can verify a bank account via micro-deposit; otherwise, we accept bank letter + voided check for initial setup.

Next steps:
1) Fill vendor form + attach W-9 (you already have that).
2) Indicate whether you prefer ACH or wire (and provide bank details).
3) Confirm remittance email and primary invoice email destination.
4) Marissa will trigger the PO enablement once details are verified.

I'll leave the schedule to Marissa/Ben — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Sales Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_vendor_form.pdf; PO_workflow_overview.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodai.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom@greenlinesys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 08:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Supplier setup — banking options, remittance & invoice flow

Tom — quick note from Procurement: we usually enable PO issuance once we have: completed vendor form, W-9, bank verification (micro-deposit or bank letter), and your standard payment terms. Our standard Net terms are Net 45 for new suppliers; we can discuss Net 30 once we have a short payment history. 

A few clarifications so Finance can code invoices correctly:
- Please include one contact for invoice disputes and one contact for remittances (they can be the same). Include direct phone and email.
- If you use multiple remit-to bank accounts, flag which one to use per invoice.
- If you require invoice approvals from a specific Redwood PO approver, note that in the vendor form.

Tom, once you return the completed vendor form, Ben will coordinate verification and we’ll add Greenline to our PO system (you’ll get a notification when first PO is issued).

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Procurement Operations

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodai.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom@greenlinesys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 12:15:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Supplier setup — banking options, remittance & invoice flow

Tom — Ben on Finance ops here. Two operational notes: 

1) Micro-deposit verification: we prefer to push two micro-deposits to the account you provide and you confirm the amounts. That reduces errors vs manual entry of bank letters. If you prefer a bank letter, upload an original PDF on company letterhead with bank routing/account obfuscated except last 4 digits.

2) Invoice metadata: mandatory fields we parse automatically — invoice number, invoice date, PO number, total, and remit-to email. If those fields are missing we have to route invoices to manual processing which delays payment.

Also: attach your vendor portal credentials if you want us to create an integration (SFTP key or API token). Otherwise email invoices@redwoodai.com with one PDF per invoice as Rachel noted.

I’ll start the vendor record once we get the completed form and verification. Expected turnaround after verification is ~6 business days for PO enablement.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Finance Operations Lead
Attachment: (none)

Questions: is Net 45 required contractually or can we request Net 30 on the first PO? Also, can you confirm whether PO numbers will be present on email subject lines of the POs we receive? 

I can schedule a 15-minute touch-base tomorrow if you want to walk through the verification.

Tom
